title: Cold rebuild: Compute a tree id
summary: Rebuild Compute a tree id from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Compute a tree id** in *Trees and commits*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A tree entry for a file is `<mode> <name>\0` plus the raw id bytes. How many bytes is this entry?
steps.explain: `100644` (6) + space (1) + `hello.txt` (9) + NUL (1) = 17, plus 20 raw bytes of SHA-1. A 40-character hex id would have been twice as long.

steps.title: Rebuild Compute a tree id cold
prompt: Write `TreeId(List<(string Mode, string Name, string Id)> entries)` that returns a real Git tree id:
1. Sort entries by name with `StringComparer.Ordinal`, but compare a directory (mode `40000`) as `name + "/"`.
2. Body = for each entry: UTF-8 bytes of `"<mode> <name>\0"` then `Convert.FromHexString(id)` (20 bytes).
3. Id = SHA-1 of `"tree <body length>\0"` + body, as lowercase hex.
The checks use the real ids of a repo holding `hello.txt` and `src/App.cs`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
static string TreeId(List<(string Mode, string Name, string Id)> entries)
